intro.text: The war begins. Somewhere in {place}, six other Masters have summoned their Servants, and every one of them is now your enemy. By day the city goes about its business. By night, it belongs to you and them.

The war begins. Somewhere in {place}, six other people with marks like yours have summoned their own heroes, and every one of them is now your enemy. By day the city goes about its business. By night, it belongs to you and them.

dawn.text: Morning comes over {place}.
Grey light creeps over the rooftops of {place}.
You wake early. The city is already stirring.
Temple bells ring across Kyoto, as they have every morning for a thousand years.
Fog lies thick on the river, and London wakes slowly underneath it.
The astronomical clock strikes the hour as Prague wakes.
The morning is already hot and heavy in New Orleans, and somewhere a trumpet is practicing scales.
Ship horns sound from the port as Buenos Aires wakes.
Milk carts rattle down the street outside your window.
The first trams of the day clatter past.
Traffic is already roaring by the time you wake.
You wake before your alarm, heart pounding from a dream you can't remember.
You wake to the smell of coffee. {servant} is pretending not to have made it.
Rain on the window. You lie still for a minute, counting the days left.
The sky turns from black to grey to a washed-out blue.
Birds start up outside before the sun is properly up.
You wake stiff and sore, and lie still for a moment, listening.
Somewhere down the street, someone is already sweeping their front step.
The air is cold and clean this morning, the kind of morning that feels like a fresh start.
A bell rings somewhere far off, counting the hour.
You wake with the Command Seals itching on your hand.
Pale sunlight crawls across the floor toward you.
The city wakes the way it always does, as if nothing happened in the night.
Mist hangs over the rooftops, slowly burning away.
{servant} is already awake, watching the street from the window.
You find {servant} asleep in a chair by the door, and let them be for a few more minutes.
"Good morning," {servant} says, as if it's an ordinary day. You almost believe it.

dusk.text: The sun goes down, and the streets of {place} empty out.
Night falls. Somewhere out there, the others are moving too.
Lamps come on one by one as darkness settles over {place}.
Gas lamps flicker to life along the street.
Neon signs buzz on, one after another, as the light fails.
The evening bells of {place} fade, and with them the last of the day.
Music starts up in the bars as the sun goes down.
{servant} checks the windows one last time, then turns to you. "Ready?"
The last light goes red over the rooftops, and the city holds its breath.
Shadows stretch long across the street, then swallow it.
The day's noise fades to a murmur, then to nothing.
You eat a quick, cold supper and check your Command Seals one more time.
The first stars come out, and with them, the war.
Windows go dark one by one across the city.
A cold wind picks up as the sun goes down.
Somewhere a dog barks, then thinks better of it.
The city exhales, and the night begins.
Clouds roll in, hiding the moon.
The streetlights come on, small islands in the dark.
{servant} straightens up as the light fades, every inch a warrior again.
"Let's see what tonight brings," {servant} says quietly.

texts.text: You spend the day resting behind locked doors while {servant} keeps watch.
You sleep late and eat well. {servant} takes the chance to rest as well.
You spend the day behind locked doors, sleeping in short, frightened stretches.
You sleep most of the day away. When you wake, {servant} is sitting by the window, keeping watch.
You force yourself to do nothing at all, which turns out to be very hard.
A quiet day of tea, mending and sleep. You'd forgotten what that felt like.

dayActions.label: Train with {servant}
dayActions.hint: Small Body and Magecraft gains, Bond +1

texts.text: {servant} puts you through a punishing day of drills. By evening you can barely lift your arms, but you are faster than you were.
You practice moving and fighting together with {servant}, until you can tell what they will do before they do it.
{servant} drills you on footwork until you can move without thinking.
You practice working magic while {servant} attacks you with a broom. It helps more than you'd like to admit.
{servant} teaches you how to fall without getting hurt, which is most of fighting, apparently.

dayActions.label: Gather intel
dayActions.hint: Mind and contacts help. Rumors can tell you a lot, but not everything

texts.text: You spend the day walking the city, listening, watching, and asking careful questions.
You check on your contacts and go through the local news for anything strange.
You walk the districts where strange things happened, looking for traces of magic.
You read every newspaper you can find, looking between the lines.
You sit in a café near the river all day, watching who comes and goes.

rumors.text: Someone at a café swears they saw a man in armor on a rooftop at midnight. Their friends laugh at them.
Three people in the old district have reported the same strange dream: a field of burning spears.
A night watchman found scorch marks on a wall that no fire could have made. He was told to forget it.
A stranger has been asking around about old houses with deep cellars.
Birds have stopped roosting in one particular park. Nobody can say why.
The local paper reports a gas leak on the east side. You have seen gas leaks. That was not one.
A grainy video online shows a flash of light over the river. It already has thousands of views.
A taxi driver swears a woman stepped out in front of his car last night, and the car bent around her.
Someone has been buying up every candle in the old quarter.
A bartender mentions a foreign gentleman who pays in very old coins.
Dogs all over the east side howled at the same moment last night.
Three windows on one street shattered at midnight. No stones were found.
A radio station went silent for ten minutes last night, and nobody can say why.
Someone posted a photo of a scorched wall online, and it was deleted within the hour.

nothing.text: Whatever the other Masters are doing, they are being careful. You find nothing useful.

maxed.text: Every rumor you hear is one you already know. To learn more about the others, you will have to see them for yourself.

dayActions.label: Prepare your workshop
dayActions.hint: Build up wards and traps at your base

texts.text: You spend the day laying wards around your base: bounded fields at the doors, alarms on the windows, and a few nastier surprises.
Following {servant}'s advice, you fortify your base as best you can: locks, tripwires, and a few charms you barely understand.
Alone, you fortify your base as best you can: locks, tripwires, and every ward you can remember.
You spend the day drawing circles in chalk and blood under the floorboards, and sealing them.
You rig the stairs so they creak in a pattern only you know.

dayActions.label: Earn some money
dayActions.hint: Odd jobs and favors. You'll need the money

texts.text: You pick up a day's work wherever you can find it.
You do a favor for one of your contacts, and they pay well.
You sell a few things you can do without.
You take a day's work in a warehouse, keeping your head down.

dayActions.label: Propose an alliance
dayActions.hint: Needs a rival whose name and base you know

texts.text: You send word to {label}, proposing that you stop fighting each other for now.

accepted.text: After a tense meeting on neutral ground, {label} agrees. For now, you are allies.

refused.text: {label} refuses. You get the impression they would rather see you dead.

dayActions.label: Spend the day with {servant}
dayActions.hint: Time together. Bond +1, and they may share something

texts.text: You set the war aside for a day and spend it with {servant}.
No plans, no scouting. Just a day with {servant}.
You let {servant} decide how to spend the day.
You and {servant} move through the dark streets, keeping to the shadows.
You patrol the rooftops and back alleys with {servant}, watching for any sign of the enemy.
Alone, you move through the dark streets, keeping to the shadows.
You walk the waterfront with {servant}, listening for anything wrong.
You cross the city by back streets and rooftops, one district at a time.

quiet.text: The night passes without incident. Whatever is out there, it doesn't show itself.
You see nothing but a stray dog and a few late drinkers heading home.
Nothing tonight. Just the city, breathing in its sleep.
A cat follows you for a while, then loses interest.
You find traces of a fight from nights ago: scorch marks, a cracked wall. Nothing new.
Somewhere far off, a siren wails and fades.

nightActions.label: Scout a known location
nightActions.hint: Watch a rival's territory up close. They may spot you

texts.text: You and {servant} slip into {district} after dark, looking for {label}.
Alone, you slip into {district} after dark, looking for {label}.

success.text: You watch from the shadows for hours. They never notice you.

spotted.text: Something gives you away. A wave of killing intent washes over the street.

nothingNew.text: You watch for hours, but learn nothing you didn't already know.

nightActions.label: Ambush a known Master
nightActions.hint: Lie in wait for a rival at their base. Their workshop will help them

texts.text: You take up position near {base} in {district} and wait for {label} to come out.
You stay inside with the lights off while {servant} keeps watch. Nobody comes.
You lie low for the night. Far away, you hear something like thunder on a clear night.
You sit in the dark with {servant}, talking quietly until you fall asleep.
You stay in, every light off, every ward up, and listen to the city.

contactTip.text: A message arrives from one of your contacts, with something they thought you should know.

finalNight.text: The fourteenth night falls. The war cannot last past dawn: tonight, the Grail will choose.

rivalsDecide.text: Across the city, the last Masters throw everything they have at each other.

lastRival.text: When the dust settles, only one rival is left standing: {label}.

allEliminated.text: There is no one left to fight. You are the last Master standing.
